title: 1972 AHSME Problem 21
statement: If the sum of the measures in degrees of angles \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) \(E,\) and \(F\) in the figure is \(90n,\) then \(n\) is equal to:

solutions.text:
Let \(P=AD\cap BF\) and \(Q=AD\cap CE.\) In quadrilateral \(EFPQ,\) \[ E+F+\angle P+\angle Q=360^\circ. \] The triangles \(BPD\) and \(AQC\) give \(B+D=\angle P\) and \(A+C=\angle Q,\) using the supplementary angles at \(P\) and \(Q.\) Adding yields \[ \begin{gathered} A+B+C+D+E+F\\ =360^\circ=90^\circ\cdot4. \end{gathered} \] Thus \(n=4.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Name the two intersections of \(AD\) with \(BF\) and \(CE\)
Combine the angle sums of the central quadrilateral and the two triangles attached to it
